cells.tense: You have the pattern and you are saying it plainly while the session is still warm.
cells.act: let yourself be drawn before you choose
cells.ask: Sit with the part of the practice that draws you right now — not the part on the plan — and begin there, without weighing whether it's the right choice.
cells.core:
The work has a direction now, and that direction belongs to you. You sit down to practise, and partway in a shape comes clear — the structure beneath the drills, not the drills themselves — and you can put it in plain words. Skill feeds understanding, understanding feeds skill back, so a session that went well shows you why it went well, and the reps stop being a wall you climb.

There is a pull inside the practice you trust before you can justify it. Follow that once. Before you begin, let yourself be drawn toward whichever part you actually want to work on, and start there. The goal isn't choosing well. It's to stop picking with the part of you that only knows what's already been done.
cells.sheetLine: You can see the pattern, not just run the drill.
cells.verb: cutting to the pattern under the words
cells.place: at the bench of your own practice, where skill is made by repetition

cells.tense: You are cutting tomorrow's pattern before tomorrow's practice has even happened.
cells.act: decide it and act the same day, without explaining
cells.ask: When a session turns into refining further than the work asks, name the whole move and do that part today, then close the day. No explaining it afterward.
cells.core:
The bench work has run past the hands. The next round is already worked out in your head — how it will go, what it will show, what it means — before any of it has been done, and the practice is no longer the point. It's the evidence. The plan gets longer, the sessions get shorter, and the pattern you keep finding is the one you carried in.

What brings you back is letting one decision finish. Not the system — one piece of the refinement you know you want, acted on today, with no account of it to anyone, including yourself. Most of what you are building before its time can wait until the work asks. Take the one thing, do it, and close it out.

cells.tense: The practice is still here and you are standing past it, at a door you already chose.
cells.act: leave the hollow ritual for the living one
cells.ask: Find the one regular slot you keep with no lift in it, and set it down this week without replacing it. Everything else stays.
cells.core:
The sessions happen. The bench is set. None of it reaches you. You can run the drills and you can't find where they're headed or why you're still at them, because you're already at the next thing — another teacher, another room, whatever comes after. Going through the motions while standing somewhere else is the worst of both.

One piece of the practice is a routine now, not a practice. Find it and stop it — a clean ending, not a taper. Then the rest can be alive, because the thing you've been hauling from habit isn't in the way. What comes next shows itself once you've set down what you were carrying past its use.
cells.sheetLine: You're still doing it and already standing past it.

cells.tense: You are running the analysis and calling it the practice, as if the looking came from nowhere.
cells.act: follow the pull of what might be felt, a little way
cells.ask: Give the thing in your practice that keeps drawing you an unhurried stretch with nothing else running, follow it a short way, and leave no notes after.
cells.core:
The reading is settled before the reading is over, and you call that the practice. The pattern-finding does real work, and your account of it says you were just following the method. It isn't the method. Something in you leans toward one part of the material over another, and you've been treating that lean as noise to be filtered out.

The lean is the beginning, not a byproduct. Give it one small stretch this week, ten minutes with nothing else running, and follow it a short way into practice you haven't done. It doesn't need to be recorded or defended. That is what it was before it was a technique — one person drawn toward one thing they couldn't look away from.
cells.sheetLine: The lean is doing the work. The method is what's on record.
